title: The Ascension of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The ascension of Christ means that the risen Jesus was taken up into heaven and exalted at the right hand of the Father. He reigns, intercedes, and will return in glory.
summary: The ascension of Christ means that the risen Jesus was taken up into heaven and exalted at the right hand of the Father. He reigns, intercedes, and will return in glory.
christFocus: Jesus is the ascended Lord who has completed His earthly mission and now reigns in heavenly glory. His ascension assures believers that their Savior is enthroned and active for them.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
After His resurrection, Jesus ascended into heaven before His disciples. His ascension was not disappearance into weakness, but exaltation into glory.

The ascended Christ is seated at the right hand of the Father. This shows authority, honor, completion of His atoning work, and His present reign over all things for the church.

His ascension also means believers have a great High Priest who has passed through the heavens. He represents His people before God and gives them confidence to draw near.

The angels told the disciples that Jesus will return in the same way they saw Him go. The ascension therefore points both to His present reign and His future appearing.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers live as though Jesus is absent or inactive. The ascension teaches that Christ is not gone in defeat; He is exalted, reigning, interceding, and preparing to return.

This doctrine strengthens prayer, mission, and courage. The church serves under the authority of the ascended Lord, not under the fear of earthly powers.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Lift your eyes to the ascended Christ. Pray with confidence, serve with courage, and live with hope because your Savior reigns at the Father’s right hand and will come again in glory.
